when: A chemical reaction arrow, or a species carrying a name or a charge off the line of the equation. Chemistry chapter 6 (organic) carries 419 of them; chapter 4 (inorganic) 81.
notes: The arrow is DRAWN with a border and a CSS arrowhead rather than typed as a glyph, so it stretches to whichever of its two labels is wider — a six-word reagent over a fixed-width arrow overhung it on both sides. Reagent above, condition below: that placement IS the answer to 'complete the equation', and printed inline it is unreadable. `overset` has two meanings and they are not styled alike: a label over an ARROW, and a charge over an ATOM, where the charge must sit tight against the letter because a carbocation's + a full line up reads as a separate term. See book/format/reaction.py for why all 500 were destroyed before this existed.
